Your experience is somebody's missing step.

Most small businesses in South Africa do not fail for lack of effort. They fail on the things nobody told them: which permit they needed, what a funder actually reads, why the price was wrong. If you have been through that, you already know enough to help.

You should register if…

  • You have run, managed or advised a business for three years or more, formal or informal.
  • You work in a field founders keep asking about: compliance, bookkeeping, food safety, construction, tenders, marketing, logistics, retail, trades.
  • You have done the paperwork yourself, CIPC registration, SARS, B-BBEE affidavits, CSD, municipal permits.
  • You have sat on the other side of the table: a funder, a procurement officer, a bank, an incubator, a training provider.
  • You can give an hour or two a month and actually show up for it.

You do not need to…

  • Be famous, wealthy, or running a big company.
  • Have a degree. Practical experience counts here.
  • Commit to long programmes. Many founders need two or three focused conversations, not a year.
  • Have all the answers. Knowing which official source to check is often the answer.
  • Charge, or work for free. You set that yourself.

Five steps, and you are matched.

1You create a mentor profile

Personal details, work experience, education, the industries and business stages you can help with, your languages, and a short bio in your own words. It takes about ten minutes.

2You go live straight away

Your profile is published as soon as you submit it. You can edit it, or pause it, from your mentor dashboard at any time.

3Founders find you

You appear in mentor matching. Founders are shown mentors whose industry, stage and language fit what they are working on right now. Not a popularity list.

4You get the request live

When a founder asks you to mentor them, an alert appears on your dashboard immediately with their business, their goal and their message. You accept or decline. You are never assigned anyone.

5You talk

Accepting opens a private chat between the two of you inside INSYTE, and a one-click video room for face-to-face sessions. If the founder chooses to share their Business health report with you, you will see it too.

What we ask of you

Be honest about your limits.

Point founders to CIPC, SARS, their municipality or a qualified professional when a question is beyond your experience. That is a good answer, not a failure.

Never promise funding or tenders.

No mentor can guarantee an outcome, and founders are told to be wary of anyone who says otherwise.

Respect what you are shown.

Business information a founder shares with you stays between you. Report sharing is consent-based and time-limited.

Show up or say so.

If you cannot take on anyone right now, pause your profile. Founders would rather see nothing than be left waiting.

For institutions

Free for founders, useful for institutions.

Public resources and basic readiness tools can remain accessible, while universities, incubators and enterprise-development programmes can pay for cohort dashboards, institutional reporting and guided support workflows.

FAQ

Questions founders usually ask first.

Is this free?

INSYTE is free for founders. Institutions may pay for cohort dashboards and support workflows.

Does INSYTE replace CIPC, SARS or professionals?

No. INSYTE gives guidance and links to official sources, but it does not replace CIPC, SARS, lawyers, accountants or mentors.

What happens to my documents?

Documents are stored against your account and protected using POPIA-aligned controls. You can request deletion at any time.

Who can see my Business health report?

Only you can see it unless you explicitly share it with a mentor for a chosen time period.

Terms of service

INSYTE is a business-readiness guidance tool. It helps users organise business information, documents, compliance tasks, funding preparation, tender preparation, mentor sharing and health check-ins.

INSYTE does not replace CIPC, SARS, municipalities, procurement officials, lawyers, accountants, financial advisors or mentors. Guidance is educational and must be verified against official sources before decisions or submissions are made.

Users are responsible for the accuracy of information and documents they enter.

You may request deletion of your data by contacting insyte.help@gmail.com.

Privacy Policy

Last updated: 25 September 2026

1. Who we are

INSYTE is a business-readiness platform for young South African entrepreneurs, built by Equitech. We help you get a business registered, compliant and ready to apply for funding and tenders.

2. What data we collect

Your name and email address. The business information you enter into the platform — your business profile, compliance checklist, documents, plans and check-ins. Usage data about how you move through the app, so we can see what is working and what is not.

3. Why we collect it

To provide the service you signed up for, to send you updates that are actually relevant to your business, and to improve the platform. We do not use your business information for anything else.

4. How we store it

Your data is stored securely via Supabase, with access rules that keep one founder's record separate from another's. We do not sell your data to third parties.

5. Your rights

You can ask for a copy of everything we hold, correct anything that is wrong, or delete your account at any time. All three are available under Settings › Account, without having to ask us first.

6. Cookies

We use essential cookies to keep you logged in — without them the app cannot work. Analytics cookies are optional and only set if you agree to them. You can change your mind at any time from the cookie banner.

7. Contact

For any privacy question, email us at insyte.help@gmail.com and a person will answer.

8. Changes to this policy

If we change anything significant here, we will email you about it rather than quietly updating this page.
